title: Performance profile attestation flow and canary hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement an end-to-end publish flow that produces a cryptographically-attested performance profile (latency/throughput/cost) and wires lightweight canary hooks in the Console so product teams can safely pin model versions. This ticket covers the policy, UX hooks, and the automation for signing, canary rollout configuration, and post-publish monitoring/auto-refresh triggers.

Scope:
- Author a publish playbook that runs from model onboarding -> profile generation -> signing -> publish to profile registry.
- Add a Console UI hook to configure canary parameters when publishing (percent, region slices, customer tiers).
- Emit attestation metadata (signer, signature, git-commit, benchmark bundle id, sampling seed) with every published profile.
- Wire canary alarms: latency P50/P95/P99, cost-per-1k-tokens, and correctness delta (from eval prompt set) with thresholds.
- Automate a soft-deprecation window and refresh path when drift triggers are detected.

Non-goals: automatic model retraining, deep model-level quality remediation, or replacing runtime routing logic (these remain with ENG runtime).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Publish playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step CLI/automation commands. 2) Profiles published to the git-backed registry include a signed attestation field and benchmark_bundle_id. 3) Console exposes canary config on publish and creates the associated rollout object. 4) Canary emits telemetry to monitoring dashboard and triggers alerting when thresholds breached. 5) A smoke run for three sample models demonstrates publish -> canary -> rollback path.
comments: 2026-03-05 @Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached. Agreed to sign profiles using company KMS + git provenance and to add a lightweight signer metadata rather than full attestation on day 1.
2026-03-07 @Marco Nguyen: Spike complete - prototype in runtime PR #4421 adds profile metadata export and a hook to sign with KMS. Local smoke shows P95 and cost metrics exported with bundle id.
2026-03-09 @Lena Ortiz (Design): Mockups for the Console canary panel uploaded. We prefer percent slider + preset region slices. Need final copy for rollback CTA.

2026-03-10 @Security (review): Security prefers sigstore-style signing for public artifacts; for now KMS-signed attestations OK if we record signer identity and commit hash. Timetable: security review complete by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 @Marco Nguyen: Integrated canary object creation in backend. Canary config stored as part of profile release metadata. Implementation draft: create 'release-canary' resource that Console can start/stop.

2026-03-12 @PM (Aisha): Notes from cross-functional review: require automated rollback when cost regression >30% or correctness delta >5% on canary traffic. Action: ENG to add rollback API and Monitoring to produce deterministic signals.
2026-03-13 @Marco Nguyen: Added auto-refresh trigger prototype that marks profile stale when drift score from telemetry pipeline > 0.15. Creating follow-up ENG ticket to backfill drift detectors.
next_steps: 1) ENG to complete PR for KMS signing and release-canary resource (ENG-4128). 2) Design to finalize text for rollback modal and presets by 2026-03-16. 3) PM to publish Confluence playbook and run three smoke publishes by 2026-03-18. 4) Security to confirm sigstore vs KMS decision and sign-off.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full sigstore adoption would give better public verification but delays delivery by ~3 weeks; KMS-signed attestations provide faster internal safety. We agreed to ship KMS-signed metadata now and schedule sigstore proof-of-concept next quarter. Canary thresholds should be conservative initially (5% traffic, 24hr ramp) to avoid noisy false positives.
audit_trail: Publish events will include timestamp, publisher, git-commit, benchmark_bundle_id, signer_id, signature_reference, and canary_id. These fields are persisted in the profile registry and surfaced in the Console audit log.
risks:
- Incorrect sampling leading to undercoverage of tail latency. Mitigation: require benchmark_bundle sampling seeds and a min-samples check.
- Signer key rotation complexity: add key rotation runbooks and signer_id mapping.
- Canary noise causing premature rollbacks: use multiple signals (latency+cost+eval) and require 3 consecutive evaluation windows before auto-rollback.
customer_impact_details: Enables customers to pin profiles with clearer trust. Short-term risk: small percentage of canaries may trigger rollbacks that require manual triage. Long-term benefit: predictable SLOs and clearer cost/latency contract for pinned model versions.
communication_plan: Announce playbook and Console feature in Platform Release notes and send targeted outreach to top five Dedicated customers. Provide a guided runbook for customers to opt into canary guardrails.
implementation_notes: - Use benchmark bundle metadata format v2. - Store signatures as opaque references to KMS envelope in registry. - Canary resource must support region-slices and tiered traffic percentages. - Monitoring: use existing telemetry contract (measurements: p50,p95,p99, cost_1k_tokens, eval_accuracy_delta).
